title: LLM runner: embed a lightweight Go LLM client for the ladder's budgeted agent stage — non-streaming completions, per-call budgets (tokens+wall-clock), config-driven model + fallback chain, context-compaction hook
description: the maintainer directive 09-16: lightweight LLM framework, avoid wastefulness — the daemon runs under stress, so STREAMING IS A NON-GOAL (one buffered request/response per stage; a hung stream is the failure mode we refuse). Plain net/http against OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoints (NO heavy SDKs — this is the lightweight framework). Config: [llm] blocks with base_url/api_key-ref/model/max_tokens/timeout per role, plus fallback_chain = ordered endpoint list; a stage tries candidates in order on transport/5xx/429 errors, records which candidate served in the ledger. Context compaction: before each stage, if the assembled context exceeds a configured budget, run a map-style compaction pass (summarize-per-chunk via the same client, single-shot, capped) and record compaction in/out token counts in the ladder record — interesting-but-accountable, never silent truncation. Skill-library support: the ladder's skills stage reads skills from a local dir in Claude-skill format (SKILL.md + frontmatter) so a REMOTE agent can author/build skills and the daemon picks them up (pull-down = git or dir mount; matches SPEC-11 skill loop + the 'remote agent will build the skill' requirement). Budgets: hard caps enforced pre-request (max_tokens) and mid-call (wall-clock timeout), over-budget = stage fails budgeted, never runaway. SPEC-05 §agent and SPEC-11 need §-amendments (letter-suffix) for the [llm] config schema + compaction contract; selfcheck must PASS.
acceptance_criteria: internal/llm client: buffered completions only (no SSE/stream), configurable endpoint/model/key-ref, timeout enforced
fallback chain: config-ordered candidates, failover on 429/5xx/transport, serving candidate recorded in the ledger stage record
context compaction hook: over-budget context triggers capped single-shot compaction, token counts recorded, never silent truncation
skills: ladder reads a local skill-library dir (SKILL.md format) and can execute a skill step against the runner
SPEC-05/11 letter-suffix amendments + selfcheck PASS
tests: client contract test (httptest server), fallback test, budget-exceeded test

title: Host-load-sensitive Go gates: `make check` / `go test ./...` are RED at fleet load_avg >= 45 (TestAmortizedThroughput 29049 vs load-derived floor 37453; TestDeriveNeverBlocks; TestCollectorLongLineIsTruncated) — make the host-measured floors load-aware at high load, or fence them out of `make check` with an explicit skip verdict
description: Found during TRBL-001 verification (2026-09-17, host load_avg 45). The v0.1 wave already made the ledger throughput floors and seven host-measured wall-clock budgets load-aware, but the load-aware form still fails ABOVE ~load 45: `go test ./... -count=1 -short` reds out in internal/research (TestDeriveNeverBlocks), internal/sentinel (TestCollectorLongLineIsTruncated) and internal/ledger (TestAmortizedThroughput, 29049 rec/s against a load-derived floor of 37453 and a spec floor of 100000 / measured 515k). `make check` therefore exits 2 and cannot be used as a pre-push gate on a busy fleet host. Verified pre-existing: the same tests fail identically on a pristine `git archive HEAD` (a6881de) control tree, so this is NOT TRBL-001 collateral. Two honest exits: (a) derive the floor from measured host capacity per run (the existing load-aware form only scales to a point) and/or make the assertion a ratio against a no-scrub baseline, or (b) split `make check` so host-measured perf gates are a separate target with an explicit SKIPPED verdict under high load, so the specs/tools gates stay a reliable gate.
acceptance_criteria: the failing tests are either green or explicitly SKIP (never silently weakened) at load_avg >= 45
any skip is recorded with the observed load_avg and the measured value, in the test output
`make check` exits 0 on a load_avg 45 host with an explicit SKIP verdict for host-measured perf gates
control-tree proof recorded: the same test ids fail identically on pre-change HEAD with no repo changes

title: [P0] The shipped examples/config.toml cannot boot: verify.zone_windows is an inline TOML table, the parser accepts only the SPEC-12 §167 k=v string - boot refuses with TROUBLE-LIFECYCLE-001 before any listener opens
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17: `cp examples/config.toml ~/dogfood-trouble/config.toml` (the path docs/cmd.md + deploy/README.md both point a new operator at) then `bin/troubled --config config.toml` refuses to boot: err="TROUBLE-LIFECYCLE-001: key \"verify.zone_windows\": bad zone_windows pair \"{\"" (exit 13, no listener, daemon never serves). examples/config.toml:65 uses TOML inline-table syntax `zone_windows = { loopback = "10m", ... }`; internal/lifecycle/config.go:433 applyToMapStringDuration accepts map[string]any OR the documented space-separated string, and the TOML decoder hands it a scalar `{`-leading string that fails the pair split. SPEC-12:167 pins the accepted form: `verify.zone_windows` default `loopback=10m lan=15m tailnet=20m public=30m`. So the example file contradicts the spec it ships with, and the FIRST key a fresh user meets is a boot refusal. Fix direction: change the example to the string form (or teach applyToMapStringDuration the inline-table shape), and add a test that boots the daemon against the shipped examples/config.toml verbatim so the example cannot rot again.
acceptance_criteria: examples/config.toml boots with the documented cc/copy/edit path (no TROUBLE-LIFECYCLE-001)

review_notes: Evidence: 401 TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002 vs 200 after the absolute token_file; token hash match; verbatim transcript in docs/dogfood/2026-09-17-integration.md.
title: [P0] Stock config yields a dashboard that can never authenticate: the default dashboard.token_file is the literal path ~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json and `~` is never expanded, so a MISSING file reads as a valid EMPTY token set - every Bearer token 401s TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002 with no log line and no health signal
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, reproduced twice on the control host. With examples/config.toml (which sets no dashboard.token_file) the daemon boots and serves :7644, but `trouble dashboard token create` mints a tdt_ token that the SAME daemon rejects: GET /incidents -> 401 {"error":{"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002","message":"authentication failed"}} - on a daemon started AFTER the token existed. The token hash in ~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json matches sha256(plaintext) exactly (verified), so mint and store agree; the daemon simply never loaded the file. Mechanism: dashboard.DefaultConfig() TokenFile = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json" (internal/dashboard/config.go:58, a literal tilde); internal/app/dashdeps.go:43 only overrides it when the lifecycle key is non-empty; nothing expands ~ inside the dashboard package, os.Stat fails, and tokens.go readFileIntoSet documents "a missing file yields a valid empty set" - so it fails closed, silently, forever. Proof of the mechanism: with the identical build, config and token, adding `token_file = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json"` to [dashboard] and restarting flips GET /incidents from 401 to 200 rendering "Incidents - trouble" (15 KB). Blast radius: the dashboard (SPEC-10) is unreachable and the ONLY credential the product can mint is inert, on the documented config path; tests/e2e/cli_smoke.sh passes only because it hands the daemon an absolute token_file. Fix direction: expand ~ (or resolve the path through the same resolver the CLI uses) in DefaultConfig/dashboardConfig, and log a WARN whenever the token store loads as missing/empty so the failure is not silent.
acceptance_criteria: a stock examples/config.toml boot accepts a CLI-minted token on /incidents (200)
the resolved token_file path is proven identical between `trouble dashboard token create` and the daemon (asserted by a test)
an empty/missing token store logs a WARN at boot (fail-closed stays, silence does not)
cli_smoke.sh gains a case that exercises the DEFAULT token_file path, not only an explicit one

review_notes: Evidence: ledger lifecycle records (verbatim in docs/dogfood/diagnostics.md), curl to :7643 = connection refused, ss shows 7643 unbound while 7644 serves. Sharpened after the rules.d-correct boot produced status="ok" with three subsystems absent.
title: [P0] Three of five subsystems are silently not built on a stock config (sentinel: no projects configured, issues: driver github needs owner+repo, skills: source_path/source_url) - the ingest on-ramp never opens and /health.json reports only a generic degraded
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17. Booting examples/config.toml writes a `subsystem_not_built` lifecycle record per refused subsystem on EVERY boot (12 records across 4 boots): sentinel: "no sentinel projects configured" (internal/app/subsystems.go:386 buildSentinel returns nil for len(projects)==0); issues: "TROUBLE-ISSUES-003: config_invalid: driver github needs owner and repo (SPEC-09 3.9.1)"; skills: "TROUBLE-SKILLS-001: config_invalid: exactly one of source_path or source_url must be set". Consequences observed: (a) nothing ever listens on ingest.bind 127.0.0.1:7643 - POST /api/1/event/ is connection-refused, so the README's headline on-ramp ("POST /api/{id}/event/, one curl from any runtime") is impossible; (b) /health.json returns status="degraded" with detail={"sensor_degraded":"inotify"} - it names a sensor, never the three absent subsystems, and has no `subsystems` key at all; (c) the dashboard surfaces nothing either, so the documented "absent means no such record" rule only works if an operator knows to grep the ledger; (d) boot exits 0 and the daemon serves, so nothing looks wrong. There is also no documented (or implemented) way to declare a project: no CLI verb, no config key reachable through `trouble config explain` - sentinel's project set is only ever passed in-process (SubsystemOptions.SentinelProjects), so an operator cannot enable the ingest plane at all. Fix direction: populate SentinelProjects from config ([[projects]] with id/public_key/secret), surface a `subsystems` block (name, built, refusal code) in /health.json + the dashboard, and make the README's on-ramp example reachable from the shipped example config. LATER SAME RUN (sharper evidence): with a rules.d installed (examples/rules/10-defaults.toml copied to <state_root>/../config/rules.d/) the daemon reports /health.json status="ok" with detail=null and all six sensors degraded=false - while the same boot's ledger still carries the three subsystem_not_built records (sentinel: no sentinel projects configured; issues: TROUBLE-ISSUES-003; skills: TROUBLE-SKILLS-001). So the health surface does not merely under-describe a degraded boot: on a clean-shaped config it issues a GREEN light for an instance whose ingest plane, issue desk and skill loop are absent. That is the project's own named anti-pattern ("never observe itself into a green lie") reproduced on the health surface, and it is why this row is P0.
acceptance_criteria: a stock boot cannot report status="ok" while any subsystem was refused (regression test over a boot with no projects configured)
a documented config surface declares projects (id + DSN public key) and the ingest listener actually binds
POST /api/{id}/event/ with the documented auth form lands one event + one group record (asserted end-to-end against a config built from examples/)
/health.json carries a per-subsystem built/refused block; the dashboard shows refused subsystems

review_notes: Evidence: doc quotes vs observed behaviour, captured in docs/dogfood/2026-09-17-integration.md (friction log).
title: [P1] No quickstart anywhere: README documents build+test but not install/run/first-event, the example config file must be repaired by hand (TRBL-005/006), and two doc strings disagree with the shipped code
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, measured against the "can a new user get to first success from the docs" question. (1) README.md has no install, no run, no config, no first-event recipe: the only commands are `go build ./...` / `go test`; a user who wants to RUN the product must find docs/cmd.md and deploy/README.md themselves. (2) Following those docs still dead-ends on TRBL-005 (example config does not parse) and TRBL-006 (minted token 401s), i.e. time-to-first-success was unbounded without reading source - three of the four blockers this run hit were docs/integration gaps, not code defects. (3) examples/trouble.env documents the dashboard bearer example as `TROUBLE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN=dsh_...` while the CLI mints `tdt_`+43 (docs/cmd.md, cli_smoke.sh:115) - the documented prefix is wrong and the env file is never read as a dashboard credential anyway (token store + IngestionKeys only). (4) docs/cmd.md says the token store keeps only `sha256(token)[:32]`; the store holds 64 hex chars (cli_smoke.sh:121 asserts 64). Fix direction: a 15-line README quickstart (make bin -> minimal config -> absolute token_file -> token create -> curl the on-ramp -> open the dashboard), fix the dsh_/tdt_ and [:32]/[:64] strings, and note that examples/config.toml must be copied AND its zone_windows form is the string form.

review_notes: Evidence: ledger aggregation by sig/inKey/kind with timestamps, quoted in docs/dogfood/diagnostics.md.
title: [P1] Idle-host amplification: 778 records / 74 incidents in 6 minutes from an idle host with 21 distinct sigs - the same sig AND same inKey re-opens a new incident 3-4x (69-142s apart) and one psi sig produced 137 event records
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, measured on a throwaway state root against the live control host (idle, loadavg ~7 but no app activity). Over 6 minutes the daemon wrote 778 ledger records: 684 event, 74 incident, 16 lifecycle, 4 config; ledger grew to 843 KB; /health.json reported events_per_min 204, groups_open 96, incidents_open 74. Only 21 distinct sigs and 21 distinct inKeys exist, yet 74 incident records - i.e. 3-4 incidents per identity: e.g. sig dbus:sha256v1:c158b3e1eac71459 with inKey ink_... at 16:02:10, 16:03:19, 16:05:41 (69s and 142s apart). SPEC/README pin the dedup+merge upsert keyed by sig+inKey with a fold inside the dedup window (AC-22) - same key, same window, new incident. Event level: one psi sig (psi:sha256v1:f8525bc3eea25477) accounts for 137 of 684 event records in 6 min, i.e. the same recurring observation is persisted every sensor cycle. The dbus storm breaker did fire ("rule:dbus_unit_failed: 21 incidents inside 5m0s"), so the breaker works while the fold does not. Projection: ~180k records/day and ~200 MB/day of ledger from ONE idle host, before any real incident; the ledger is append-only, git-distributed and auto-filed, so this growth is permanent. Ask: verify the dedup fold (window values, key derivation, upsert path) and add a per-rule event fold/suppression so a repeating condition is one record with a count, not N records.
acceptance_criteria: a repeated detection with identical sig+inKey inside the dedup window yields ONE incident (test over the real ingest/sensor path)
a repeating rule does not persist one event record per cycle (fold or counter, with the disposition visible)
measure and record records/day + ledger bytes/day on an idle host; compare against an explicit budget
no regression in storm-breaker behaviour (breaker still opens on the configured rate)

review_notes: Evidence: raw HTML captures + 401/429 bodies; transcript in docs/dogfood/2026-09-17-integration.md.
title: [P2] Dashboard polish from real use: footer renders an empty version (`trouble v ()`), the budget panel's first server render after boot is blank/zero (fills ~2s later), and the auth-failure throttle 429s a VALID token after prior failures from the same IP
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, all three observed live on a throwaway state root (autonomy=shadow). (1) Every page footer renders `trouble v () - read-mostly dashboard (SPEC-10)` while /health.json reports version c363daf / git_sha c363daf and the budget partial renders "c363daf c363daf" - the footer's version value is empty at render time, so the operator's most visible build stamp is missing while the build is correctly stamped elsewhere. (2) The /incidents page fetched immediately after boot server-renders the budget panel with empty values (`binary`/`rss`/`ledger`/`events` blank, groups open 0, incidents open 0) in the SAME response whose header says "open incidents (74)"; 9 s later /partials/budget carries the real numbers (13.7 MB, 96 groups, 74 incidents). First paint therefore contradicts itself until the first poll lands - and the numbers ARE available (runtime_watermarks in the same /health.json). (3) The auth-failure throttle keys on the client IP, not the credential: after 8-10 failed attempts from one IP (a mistyped/rotated token, or the pre-fix 400s), requests carrying a VALID token get 429 {"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-012","message":"rate limited","detail":"auth_failure_throttle"} with Retry-After: 1 for the whole 60s window. Fix direction: render the version into the footer from the same accessor the health surface uses; seed the first budget render from the same watermark source; and either key the failure throttle on (IP + credential class) or surface a distinct banner so a legitimate operator understands they are throttled, not rejected. (4) heartbeat.json is written with ledger_last_seq=0 and ledger_last_ts="" on every heartbeat - observed across three instances including one whose ledger held 188 records - so the liveness surface a human or an external monitor reads reports a permanently zero sequence while the ledger is advancing (check-stall uses the ledger directly and is unaffected; the field is simply always empty). Fold the same fix as (1): source these values from the accessors that already answer correctly elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: footer shows the version/git_sha the health surface reports
a page fetched within the first seconds after boot renders budget values consistent with its own header counts
a valid token is not throttled by failures it did not make (or the throttle response is distinguishable from auth rejection)
